property_summary: For any interfaceId, if C reports the id as supported then it must also report support for IERC165 (any supported interface implies ERC165 support); the mutant removes the super disjunct so it reports IAccessControl as supported while denying IERC165, breaking the implication.

For every bytes4 id, C.supportsInterface(id) must be true exactly when id is the IAccessControl interfaceId or the IERC165 interfaceId (and false otherwise); the mutant drops the IERC165 disjunct so it returns false for IERC165, violating the characterization.

For every bytes4 interfaceId, C either does not support interfaceId at all, or it also reports support for IERC165 (ERC165 self-support is implied by any supported interface); the mutant supports IAccessControl while denying IERC165, so for interfaceId = IAccessControl the disjunction fails.

For every bytes4 interfaceId, C.supportsInterface(id) returns true exactly when id is the IAccessControl interface id or the IERC165 interface id; the mutant drops the ERC165 disjunct, so it returns false for id == type(IERC165).interfaceId where the reference returns true.

For every bytes4 id, C.supportsInterface(id) is true iff id is the IAccessControl or the IERC165 interface id; the mutant drops the super disjunct, so it returns false for IERC165's interface id where the reference returns true.

For any bytes4 interfaceId, supportsInterface must return true exactly for the IAccessControl interface id (plus the inherited IERC165 id); the mutant checks IERC165 instead of IAccessControl, so it returns false for the IAccessControl id, breaking the rule for that fuzzed input.

property_summary: For any fuzzed address that was never granted a role, c.hasRole(PROPOSER_ROLE, account) must return false (a non-member is not a member); the mutant inverts the lookup and returns true for such accounts, breaking the rule.

For any of the three configured roles (TIMELOCK_ADMIN_ROLE, PROPOSER_ROLE, EXECUTOR_ROLE), getRoleAdmin must return the stored TIMELOCK_ADMIN_ROLE set in the constructor, but the mutant returns DEFAULT_ADMIN_ROLE instead, so the rule breaks for PROPOSER_ROLE and EXECUTOR_ROLE.

For any role other than TIMELOCK_ADMIN_ROLE (whose stored admin is itself), c.getRoleAdmin(role) returns the stored adminRole (bytes32(0) for unconfigured roles) and never equals the queried role itself; the mutant returns the role itself, breaking this for e.g. any unconfigured nonzero role.
